newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise after FOMC but off day highs - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise after FOMC but off day highs - Sept 24.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose in busy trade Tuesday, but came off their highs after the initial euphoria of stable U.S. interest rates wore off.

"The market was strong just after the announcement and then fell back. It was a bit disappointing, but there must be more long positions in the market than we thought," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee opted Tuesday for no change in rates.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.30 to 118.00, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/8 to 83-1/8. The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional 2 due 2007 rose $0.55 to 102.00.
The "Pre 2" rose to as much as 118.95 just after the FOMC announcement.
Argentine bonds had discounted a 25-basis-point U.S. rate hike, and "the uncertainty of U.S. rates now continues," said another trader at an Argentine bank.
That means the market once again may focus slavishly on upcoming U.S. economic indicators for an idea of what the FOMC will do when it next meets on November 13.
All the same, for now steady U.S. rates should be supportive for Argentine bonds as investors seek higher yields.
Traders expect a quiet session Wednesday in anticipation of the 36-hour general strike by unions on Thursday protesting the government's economic policies.
In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 5.50 percent from 5.63 percent.
